title: QUERY RUNTIME FOR MULTI-LAYER COMPOSITION OF QUERIES
technical_field: The present disclosure relates generally to database management systems, and more specifically to optimizing SQL queries that involve complex compositions of queries, such as those utilizing nested Common Table Expressions (CTEs).
background_art: Modern database management systems (DBMS) provide robust capabilities for data storage and retrieval, often supporting Structured Query Language (SQL) for querying and data management. SQL's flexibility allows for complex data manipulation, including features like Common Table Expressions (CTEs). However, not all SQL engines support advanced functionalities like nested CTEs, and optimizing queries with CTEs can be challenging. Materializing intermediate results can improve performance but may lead to increased runtime and data duplication. There is a need for a technical solution to enhance SQL querying capabilities, especially for nested CTEs, and to improve the efficiency and performance of complex SQL scripts.
summary_of_invention: The present disclosure describes a system and method for optimizing SQL queries, particularly those with nested Common Table Expressions (CTEs). The system includes a SQL optimization engine that receives SQL scripts, processes them through three stages (CTE normalization, materialization, and caching), and outputs optimized SQL to a query engine. The CTE normalization stage unnests nested CTEs into single-level CTEs. The materialization stage uses a materialized Create Table As Select (CTAS) strategy for the base query. The caching stage allows for reusability of the materialized base query across multiple queries, enhancing efficiency and performance. This system addresses limitations in SQL engines lacking native support for nested CTEs, improving query performance and management of large datasets.
brief_description_of_drawing: FIG. 1 is a block diagram illustrating a system for optimizing SQL queries. FIG. 2 illustrates a tree data structure representative of an SQL script containing multiple CTEs. FIG. 3 is a flow diagram illustrating a method for flattening an SQL script that includes nested common table expressions. FIG. 4 is a flow diagram illustrating a method for materializing an SQL script. FIG. 5 is a method illustrating a caching mechanism for SQL scripts. FIG. 6 is a block diagram of a computing device.
detailed_description: The detailed description outlines a system and method for optimizing SQL queries, focusing on nested Common Table Expressions (CTEs). The system comprises a SQL optimization engine that receives SQL scripts from a SQL editor application and outputs optimized SQL to a query engine for execution on a database. The optimization engine operates in three primary stages: CTE normalization, materialization, and caching. The CTE normalization stage unnests nested CTEs into single-level CTEs. The materialization stage implements a materialized Create Table As Select (CTAS) strategy for the base query. The caching stage enables reusability of the materialized base query across multiple queries, thereby increasing efficiency and performance. This system provides technical solutions to enhance SQL engines that lack native support for nested CTEs, leading to improved query performance and better management of large datasets. The document further details various implementations of these methods, including parsing SQL scripts, building hierarchical representations, traversing CTEs, renaming CTEs to avoid name collisions, identifying CTEs for materialization based on prefixes, converting CTEs to CTAS statements, and optimizing query execution through materialization and caching. It also describes the components of the system, such as the SQL editor, query builder, query engine, and databases, as well as the hardware architecture of a computing device that can implement these methods.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein flattening the plurality of CTE statements comprises: parsing the SQL script to build a hierarchal representation of the SQL script; and traversing the hierarchal representation to flatten the CTE statements included in the SQL script.

4. The method of claim 3, wherein renaming the one or more of the plurality of CTE statements comprises renaming the one or more of the plurality of CTE statements upon detecting a name collision.

5. The method of claim 1, wherein materializing at least one of the plurality of CTE statements comprises analyzing names associated with the plurality of CTE statements to identify the at least one of the plurality of CTE statements to materialize.
6. The method of claim 5, wherein analyzing names comprises determining if a name of the at least one of the plurality of CTE statements includes a predefined prefix.

abstract: The present disclosure describes a system and method for optimizing SQL queries, specifically addressing challenges in handling and optimization of nested Common Table Expressions (CTEs). The system comprises a SQL optimization engine configured to receive SQL scripts from a SQL editor application and output optimized SQL to a query engine for execution on a database. The optimization engine utilizes three primary stages: a CTE normalization stage, a materialization stage, and a caching stage. The CTE normalization stage unnests nested CTEs into single-level CTEs. The materialization stage implements a materialized Create Table As Select (CTAS) strategy for materializing the base query. The caching stage enables reusability of the materialized base query across multiple queries, increasing efficiency and performance. This system provides technical solutions to enhance the capabilities of SQL engines that lack native support for nested CTEs, offering improved query performance and management of large datasets.
